# Title
#   Study_Name: VM19-193, Indian Ocean, 250,000 year long biomarker reconstructions
#---------------------------------------
# Investigators
#   Investigators: Windler, Grace; Tierney, Jessica E.; deMenocal, Peter B.
#---------------------------------------
# Description_Notes_and_Keywords
#   Description: Leaf wax dD and d13C, alkenone SST, GDGT Sub-T data and reconstructions from marine core VM19-193 in the equatorial western Indian Ocean that extends 250 ky
#         Provided Keywords: Indian Ocean, leaf wax, temperature, Pleistocene paleoclimate, monsoon, shelf exposure
#---------------------------------------
# Publication
#   Authors: Windler, Grace, Tierney, Jessica E., and deMenocal, Peter B.
#   Published_Date_or_Year: 2023-02-01
#   Published_Title: Hydroclimate variability in the equatorial western Indian Ocean for the last 250,000 years
#   Journal_Name: Paleoceanography and Paleoclimatology
#   Volume: 38
#   Edition: 
#   Issue: 2
#   Pages: 
#   Report_Number: e2022PA004530
#   DOI: 10.1029/2022PA004530
#   Online_Resource: 
#   Full_Citation: 
#   Abstract: Indian Ocean sea surface temperatures (SSTs) impact precipitation across the basin through coupled responses to climate perturbations. To understand the hydroclimate response over the western Indian Ocean and equatorial east Africa to different forcing mechanisms, we present four new proxy reconstructions from core VM19-193 (2.98° N, 51.47° E) that span the last 250ky. Sub-surface water temperatures (Sub-T; TEX86) show strong precessional (23 ky) variability that is primarily influenced by maximum incoming solar radiation (insolation) during the Northern Hemisphere spring season, likely indicating that local insolation dominates the upper water column at this tropical location over time. Leaf waxes, on the other hand, reflect two different precipitation signals: d13Cwax (in phase with boreal fall insolation) is likely reflecting vegetation changes in response to local rainfall over east Africa, whereas dDprecip (primarily driven by boreal summer insolation) represents changes in regional circulation associated with the summer monsoon. Glacial-interglacial changes in ocean temperatures support glacial shelf exposure over the Maritime Continent in the eastern Indian Ocean and the subsequent weakening of the Indian Walker Circulation as a mechanism driving 100 ky climate variability across the tropical Indo-Pacific. Additionally, the 100 ky spectral power in dDprecip supports a basin-wide weakening of summer monsoon circulation in response to glacial climates. Overall, the proxy records from VM19-193 indicate that both precession and glacial-interglacial cycles exert control over hydroclimate at this tropical location.
